verdict.tagline: Huge tactical battles buried beneath performance hurdles and steep learning curves.
for_you_if: you crave deeply coordinated tactical warfare
you coordinate squad actions using voice chat
you possess endless patience for steep learning curves
not_for_you_if: you expect smooth frame rates on release hardware
you lack the patience for long walks across maps
you get frustrated by connection errors and empty servers
you need robust in-game tutorials to start playing

citations.review_text: I have hundreds of hours on this on my Xbox series s and it ran pretty badly but I put up with it because it was a series s and I knew it sucked. claims.claim: Reviewers state that the user interface is poorly designed and confusing to navigate when attempting to change classes or squads.

citations.review_text:
Harder to get into than Fort Knox.

- Average gameplay experience will consist of getting sniped immediately after spawning-in, or running to a battle  to support your team only to then get sniped instantly from someone you can't even see.
- Players will consist of veterans with an average of at least 200+ hours and will be speaking an entirely different language to you, "why don't we have any nodes?", "neutralize on outpost", "AD at garrison". 
- Guns variety is very limited. Only ~ three types of gun: rifle, smg, shottie. Classes are virtually identical.
- UI is terrible. Trying to swap to a different class is a nightmare. Any other class-based game I've played like TF2 or Planetside 2 lets you instantly click and select the class you want. I have no idea how or why I need to make a squad to change or who's my leader or what my team is supposed to be doing. I follow my team but then we either get bombed, strafed, or sniped.
- Map variety sucks. Apparently there's more than 10 but the game kept putting me either in a city or a beach. I think there were two city maps which were different but they looekd identical.
- Game is very hard to read. I remember walking over to one of our spawn/ objective/ garrison/ checkpoint points (I dunno, there were crates everywhere) and staring at a guy - who stared at me for about a minute. I thought he was friendly (everyone wears the same drab-grey uniform), then he suddenly headshots me....wtf? He was a baddie?

Everyone on voice chat sounds like they're attending a boardroom meeting on Teams to discuss the stock forecast for the next quarter of the fiscal year.  I know there must be a game somewhere in here but I don't want to have to study an online masters degree to 'get with it'. Why can't I just hop in and play and have fun? Battlefield was nowhere this complicated or messy. Also the graphics kinda suck.

I like the concept of this game, but the execution is horrible, and feels intentionally inaccessible to most players outside of their sweaty hardcore audience. Just because it is meant to be "lighter" than ARMA or Squad (other MILSIM games I don't like), doesn't mean it will actually be more welcoming or more fun to new players. Basically, it's not fun, and don't waste your time and money trying to figure it out unless you are already someone who likes the hardcore MILSIM experience.

This game, Hell Let Loose, is just another boring MILSIM/walking simulator that is extremely hostile to new players in terms of both a toxic community, and the unintuitive gameplay itself, with plenty of annoying jank and bad optimization to make a STALKER game blush. While I did not experience cheaters in my game during my short playtime of HLL, it should be noted that it remains a significant problem that many others have consistently mentioned. If you want something similar in concept that is not another boring and frustrating MILSIM, try out Rising Storm 2, that old game still seems better than the new Vietnam game coming out of the HLL series.

Also, the UI is trash. Information/HUD overload, and the game expects you to already understand, or be a really quick learner, or else you will have a miserable time being confused and clueless when playing. The overall learning curve of HLL is too steep to actually have fun and feel like a game. It's not worth the time and trouble of trying to learn it. Apparently the transfer of the IP's ownership to Team17 has only made HLL even worse anyway.

I would rather just keep playing Battlefield 4 and Insurgency Sandstorm for my usual military/tactical FPS rotation, old but gold. I have never really been a fan of most MILSIM games anyway, and HLL is no exception. There is a new MILSIM title that I have had a better experience with that is being run by some big names in the tactical shooter sphere, but I would rather not give them a shoutout or r…

claims.claim: Reviewers report performance issues including stuttering and inconsistent frame rates across different maps and settings.

citations.review_text: Game is unplayable due to constant stutter. Never had a game with this piss poor performance. Pathetic developers.

Being a main competitor of Squad 44 it was worth giving this a try, and despite strong player numbers and wide variety of maps, the game is considerably more shallow than it might seem at first.

"Being a Hardcore/Realistic Shooter" is fails to implement seemingly most basic features that one could expect:
• No Range control on weapons
• Can't pick up weapons from dead soldiers
• No Fire Control modes
• No ammo check
• No prone movement when ads
• No Hip fire with machineguns (without first having to "grab" the handle

It's kind of ironic that apart from visuals, game mechanics this one falls short of even Rising Storm series, which is by now over 10 years old.

From immersion we also have weird choices. Faction equipment is same no matter where and when you fight. This means that STG-44 (the year of manifacture is in the name) and other equipment can be found on fronts in time periods where it has no right to exist.  If they could tie equipment and vehlicle selection to each map scenario then it would be interesting.

So after first 10 games, you realise that you have kind of seen everything that game has to offer.

Performance wise.... It's good and awful. Optimization is all over the place: 
• Omaha Beach:  150 FPS - Epic settings
• Remagen (with rain): 20-60fps - Medium settings + stuttering.

Overall random stutters appears to be the gimmick of this product. Whether that is the issue of Proton layer is yet to be seen. 

The usage of Inertia movement is good by itself, but especially annoying when many hitboxes on maps haven't been properly implemented. Amount of times that I got killed because my character gets stuck behind a tree branch, random rubble or walls that they clearly should have no issue passing through was more than agitating. 

From gameplay perspective some weird selections are also there. Why aren't there tickets per team? Why defence timers don't progress over to next point? It kind of removes a lot of tactical and strategical play that could m…

citations.review_text: Fun game with good gameplay. Sadly it still lacks in reasons to play the game for. You really can't unlock alot of cosmetics or weapons so playing the game can feel quite pointless, since you won't unlock anything. Still would recommend.

Yet another entry into the Red Orchestra style of World War 2 shooters, and Hell Let Loose doesn't do anything particularly well compared to other titles in the genre. It doesn't do anything revolutionary, or ground breaking, and in reality it's a clone of Post Scriptum and Red Orchestra 2 with a slightly more in depth progression system underneath it. 

The core gameplay loop, if you break it down into its absolute most basic parts, is very solid. It's basically a clone of Red Orchestra 2, Rising Storm, Squad/Post Scriptum(Squad 44 now), Battlefield etc. , with some small differences. [b] However [/b] this is where I find the positives to stop. When a game is designed with progression in mind a player with limited time to utilize the product should not be punished for having said limited time. Hell Let Loose locks, in many cases, superior weapons or loadouts behind level caps for different classes, and while there isn't a super long grind for each level of a given class, the issue arises when you have to leave a match early.

When you sit down and play the game, there is no quick join option to put you into a nearly full or rapidly filling server, and instead you have to find a server on your own. Most servers fall into one or two categories, already full, or empty. The full servers have a queue system that is limited to 6 people, which means if you're trying to join a server that has a group of your friends on it, you may be waiting for quite some time. This wait time is exacerbated by the progression system. In order to receive experience for your classes in game, you must be in the lobby when the game ends, which means if you play for 45 minutes, but have to leave before the game ends all of the progression you attained during that match, is lost. Why the developers felt it acceptable to institute such a flawed progression system is beyond me, and it's really the crux of the issue I have with the game. 

I wouldn't recommend this game to anyone who has limited t…

citations.review_text: Gameplay is good. But the numerous known underwhelming optimizations and bugs persistsed over the years remained unfixed making the game unplayable. For example often stuck in loading screen into the server, underoptimization causing severe framerate stutters.

Okay, here is the truth, If you want to purchase this game and ejoy it.

Issue 01 - Poorly optimized settings, TIP - go on reddit to help you or steam community to aid you in fixing some of the resolution issues (blurry, grainy views) and fps issues one example would be the -dx12 not working in game (It will be a smoother experience and your joy will increase once you apply those fixes trust me). 
Issue 02 - Lower resolution like 1080p will be at disadvantage massively, I have use this resolution as this is an old game now but considering im now using 5k ultrawide I have EXTREME advantage regarding sighting targets in distance and clearly able to see targets infront of me. Utrawide is the OP way to go here.
Issue 03 - This is for you new players please, PLEASE dont go leadership roles your dont simply understand the game yet, just follow experienced players ranks above 200+ watch them closely you'll learn alot and have a lower D in the K/D  ratio (Maybe).
Last issue 04 -  Is the current developers. We have a new developer or owner of the franchise/game and I do question if they actually understand this game or not. A change in developers means slower updates to be released and additionally they created HLL Vietnam and its BETA launch was a failure. Because of all of this I seriously question the future of this game.

Its a great game, fantastic teamwork (when it works) and alot of fun. Very competative aswell. I rate it 7.5/10.

Played 350 hrs. Game is buggy, animations are not smooth or don't work. Game physics are wonky. some maps are badly optimised. Game is fun, it strikes a good balance between realism shooters and casual shooters. Performance issues could partly be due to my outdated pc hardware, but I think it just magnifies the issues that are present. Hard to find servers and ping is always high(US west coast) seeding can take up to an hour. Server list ping is always innacurate once I am in game it always doubles i.e if server list says 30 ping in game ping is 60.

If you dont like dying repeatedly and not knowing at all where it came from this is not the game for you... if you like being kicked repeatedly in the junk this is the game for you! I will be purchasing the Vietnam version when it releases cause I am sure that will be better right......?  Right?

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the server browser is unhelpful and finding functional servers with low ping can be difficult.

citations.review_text: Played 350 hrs. Game is buggy, animations are not smooth or don't work. Game physics are wonky. some maps are badly optimised. Game is fun, it strikes a good balance between realism shooters and casual shooters. Performance issues could partly be due to my outdated pc hardware, but I think it just magnifies the issues that are present. Hard to find servers and ping is always high(US west coast) seeding can take up to an hour. Server list ping is always innacurate once I am in game it always doubles i.e if server list says 30 ping in game ping is 60.
Gameplay is fun, some maps are not. Biggest issue is UE4 randomly crashing and useless server browser.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe matches as heavily impacted by cheating, including wallhacks, ESP, map sharing, and players collaborating across opposing teams.

citations.review_text:
I use to really enjoy playing HLL and when people called out "cheater" I usually passed it off as a skill gap, mechanics of the game and inexperience, tough there were some obvious cheaters it was mostly a fun game experience.  But now as of July 2026 the game is just infested.  Wallhacks, ESP and Map Sharing is just too apparent.  Most matches are a one sided team stack with little to no coms that last maybe 30 minutes.

TLDR; "WAS" fun, now cheater infested, matches suck. Save your money and time. Hard Pass !

Great game but after playing 954hrs the cheating has got really bad. Yes I have seen auto aim etc. But the last game I played every node, tank and garrison was destroyed after mins of being created. Because smart people worked out if they have a mate or another computer on the opposing team they can spy and takeout every garrison, node and tank in record time. I played one game were RPG teams surround tanks as soon as they entered the battle field. You can tell when cheating is happening when players highlight enemy garrisons and tanks without any of the team being able to see enemy positions. Sadly I wont buy hell let loose Vietnam as the same will happen.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that progression through classes is very slow and locks important loadouts behind high level requirements.

citations.review_text: Really fun game if you like teamwork over individual skill to win matches, the grind to unlock new loadouts is long but the starter weapons and gear are still really good, lots of different classes that all demand different gameplay, one of the best game communitys ive ever played with, they are super welcoming everyone is always open to teching new players the basics.

I would have recommended this game a year or two ago but now I wouldn't buy the game unless it is on sale. Not that you won't have some fun, but you will run into a lot of frustrating issues. 

People not building garrisons or putting down outposts. You may find yourself ALWAYS playing squad leader because no one else will play the role well enough to put spawn locations down. People not using ANY comms. Not pings or marking anything. Just running to their deaths and then spawning to do it again. People not playing out their roles. Players locking out squads to be a solo tank. 

Do you like playing sniper/recon? 
Good luck if your computer loads slowly because the two Recon squads go quick. Shooting at high ping players at range requires you to lead them differently than normal latency players in the map which can be frustrating.

Progression through classes is awfully slow, and some of the best kits are locked behind these class level requirements. Loadouts are locked to specific roles. The base skins make you stand out like a sore thumb on almost every map and most times of day. One of my biggest class issues is there is a leaf sight on the AT rocket launchers, but you can't use it at all to range your shots. 

Want to play with your friends? 
Well, there is no way to group up in the menu and you will most likely end up waiting in a queue to try to get in a server together. Even then you are probably not going to be able to join the same faction. Playing with your friends will be frustrating and time consuming.

The original set of maps are the best maps to play. They run relatively well and don't have as many geometry issues when trying to traverse the maps. Though be ready to die A LOT. There are many spots on maps that are highly efficient and difficult to detect so you may find yourself getting killed by the same player repeatedly.

The British maps are poorly optimized. Weather effects make FPS plummet and driving vehicles around the African maps is a jittery…

Have you ever died to a bush 10 times and enjoyed it? I have. The thing is, once you kill said bush, you will enter nirvana. 

I mainly play shooters and this is my favorite. I'm interested in WWII and this game makes you feel like you're there. A true PTSD simulator. There are so many different roles to play. All with their own levels to grind and tactics to learn. I keep coming back to try a new class, and pop some gerrys. 

Unfortunately, the resolution isn't great on my setup, and sometimes the servers are spotty. Team mates without mics are annoying, because there is a lot of strategy in this game. Sometimes it is hard to get a squad leader who will place spawns. This leads to some matches being lopsided. Still love the game though.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game features a steep learning curve and requires tactical positioning rather than standard first-person shooter run-and-gun reflexes.

citations.review_text:
There are two possibilities as a tanker:

- You go for a flank, take 10 minutes to get in position and then get introduced to a small box of explosives with a fuse that doesn't like you being alive very much

- You are him, you singlehandedly win the entire game and you're unstoppable. AP bouncing off your armour while yours removes the father of 4 on the other end of the shell.

Infantry also exists and is amazing. Gun design, suppression mechanics, role selection and the opportunity to fill any role you want from building bunkers to mowing down fields of men with an MG42.

The main downside to this game is if you're looking for something as fast paced as conventional hero shooters/FPS games such as call of duty, you'll take some time learning how to position but once you do this is the best realistic WW2 shooter out there.

This game is so much fun.  Lots of different roles to play for your team.  I enjoy the squad based aspect and overall game play experience.  Learning curve is a bit steep at the beginning but it doesn't take too long to get the hang of things.
